body.summary: Six humans have been uploaded into a brightly coloured virtual circus and given toy bodies they cannot leave; the ringmaster Caine, an AI, runs adventures to keep them sane while his assistant Bubble watches. The newest arrival, Pomni, spends the early episodes panicking and hunting for an exit, then settles into uneasy companionship with the others as their memories of the real world erode. Episodes alternate between ensemble comedy and single-character studies, and the back half reveals the circus is built on neural scans of dead or dying people, that Kinger helped build Caine, and that abstraction is the fate awaiting anyone who breaks. ||The finale has the group confront Caine and the truth of their situation; the circus is not escaped so much as accepted, with the guests choosing to keep each other company in a world they cannot leave.||

arcs.summary: Pomni arrives, panics, watches Kaufmo abstract, and fails to find a working exit.
A candy-kingdom adventure lets Pomni bond with Gummigoo, who learns he is an NPC and is deleted by Caine.
Pomni and Kinger are paired in a haunted manor and Kinger's steadiness in the dark comes through.
Jax's cruelty and the group's strain come to a head in a baseball-themed adventure.
The circus's origin surfaces: neural scans, Kinger's role in building Caine, and what abstraction means.

themes: escapism and the impossibility of leaving

notable_scenes.summary: Pomni opens the EXIT door and finds only the Void.
Kaufmo, abstracted, is shoved down into the cellar.
Gummigoo realises he is an NPC and Caine erases him in front of Pomni.
Kinger calms in the dark of Mildenhall Manor and steadies Pomni.
Jax's needling pushes the group past patience at the baseball stadium.
The neural-scan database and the truth of the circus are laid out.
